edges.description: The mutant microRNA causes photoreceptor loss through apoptosis when injected into medaka fish. Which mis-repressed targets drive this is unknown.

miR-204 regulates dorsoventral patterning of the developing retina, and its loss in medaka causes optic fissure coloboma through elevated Meis2. How the seed variant disturbs optic fissure closure in patients has not been tested; the fish result is from knockdown, not from the patient allele.
miR-204 is required for lens development in medaka. The link from the seed variant to early-onset cataract has not been studied.

Light sensitivity is a usual consequence of cone dysfunction, but in the 2-year-old carrier it was present while the fundus was still normal, so it may precede visible degeneration, and iris coloboma may also contribute by letting excess light into the eye.
The patient allele causes photoreceptor apoptosis in vivo.
edges.limitations: Injection overexpresses the microRNA in embryos rather than expressing one mutant allele from the endogenous locus, and fish target sites differ from human ones, so the mis-repressed targets may differ.

edges.description: Loss of miR-204 impairs RPE function and retinal responses.
edges.limitations: A homozygous null allele, whereas patients carry one altered-target allele interpreted as gain of function. The defect is primarily in the RPE rather than a primary photoreceptor apoptosis.

nodes.description: A single-nucleotide change in the seed region of mature miR-204, the sequence that selects target mRNAs. The mutant microRNA represses an altered set of transcripts; in silico analysis predicts hundreds of new targets. The original authors interpret the effect as gain of function. Whether loss of repression of normal miR-204 targets also contributes is not settled (see the discussion).

biological_processes: miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional gene silencing, with altered target specificity

evidence.snippet: By linkage analysis and exome sequencing, we identified a previously undescribed heterozygous mutation, n.37 C > T, in the seed region of microRNA-204 (miR-204), which segregates with the disease in all affected individuals.

nodes.description: Medaka embryos injected with the mutant microRNA lose rods and cones through increased apoptosis, a phenotype the authors describe as consistent with the family.

nodes.description: Progressive retinal dystrophy, reported as retinal dystrophy in the original family, early-onset chorioretinal dystrophy in the Czech family and retinitis pigmentosa in the Chinese family. Age at onset varies: the Chinese proband had poor vision since childhood, while his mother began losing vision in her 30s. The retinal disease may appear with age: the proband's 2-year-old son had coloboma and photophobia but a normal fundus, which the authors attribute, tentatively, to his young age.
